notice: Easy Mode dramatically simplifies the process of filter selection, an otherwise nuanced topic. Only a few of HQPlayer's filters are accessible here, so think of Easy Mode like training wheels and don't be afraid to experiment.

help.title: Easy Mode, explained
help.body:
Pick the preset that suits your material. The Perfect Ten, Lifelike, and Damage Control are the most all-purpose presets; Old School, The Purist, and Concert Hall are excellent with the appropriate material; The Crucible, Full Analog, and Textbook are curiosities for the sake of comparison. In SDM output mode, the last three are conditional on your DAC's support for 48 kHz family DSD rates, so don't worry if you don't see them... the others are better anyway!

Emphasis can be set between 'Space' and 'Transients' on some presets; this adjusts between linear and minimum phases, respectively.

Linear phase emphasizes spatial reproduction by ensuring all frequencies arrive at the same time; it pays for this with an unnatural side-effect called pre-ringing, or smearing the transient into the time before it occurs.

Minimum phase side-steps pre-ringing, making transients sound more natural; it pays for this by delaying higher frequencies more than lower, marring the sense of space.

Choose 'Space' for live or acoustic performances where the room or venue is part of the recording. Choose 'Transients' for multi-track studio material, which often has an artificial sense of space but strong transient content. This is far from a hard rule, so experiment with both and find what sounds best to you.

When listening to high-rate material above 48 kHz (i.e., 88.2 kHz and up), switching to The Perfect Ten or Lifelike gives you special optimized "hi-res" filters. Note that in the context of HQPlayer, 'hi-res' means high-*rate*, not any 24-bit content.

When listening to lossy streams or files like MQA or MP3, toggle the button in the top right of the Easy Mode card to Lossy. This switches the first two presets to special hi-res and lossy-optimized filters; for Damage Control, it switches to filters even more highly optimized for lossy content.

The glyphs (A), (1/2), and (No) indicate the error correction (apodizing) level; if half or no correction sounds harsh and/or generates an apodizing events warning, try a different setting.

Cost pips estimate resource consumption relative to the others on this card. These are highly relative rankings; the real load depends on your hardware, your output rate, and the rest of the chain, where the modulator or DAC correction can outweigh the filter load entirely. Your mileage may vary.

Still can't decide? Experiment! Presets can be changed live at any time with only a brief interruption to playback.

emphasis.space: Choose 'Space' for live or acoustic performances where the room or venue is part of the recording. This is far from a hard rule, so experiment with both and find what sounds best to you.
emphasis.transients: Choose 'Transients' for multi-track studio material, which often has an artificial sense of space but strong transient content. This is far from a hard rule, so experiment with both and find what sounds best to you.

material.sub: Set to the current source material; 'Lossy' shows only lossy (and hi-res) optimized filters.

perfect-ten.title: The Perfect Ten
perfect-ten.description: Does everything well, no strings attached: the best-case solution to the tension at the heart of filter design.

lifelike.title: Lifelike
lifelike.description: Puts the focus on natural, realistic timbre.

old-school.title: Old School
old-school.description: Pairs well with classic-era analog recordings.

purist.title: The Purist
purist.description: Passes the original samples through unchanged. Only for the highest technical quality source material.

damage-control.title: Damage Control
damage-control.description: Aggressive clean-up; great for loudness war-era and other less-than-good material.

full-analog.title: Full Analog
full-analog.description: Imitates the smooth and relaxing sound of an analog playback chain.

textbook.title: Textbook
textbook.description: The sound of most standard-issue DAC hardware.

concert-hall.title: Concert Hall
concert-hall.description: Heavily emphasizes space over transients; for material like live classical with minimal transient content.

correction.label: Error correction
correction.tip: Disabling error correction reduces resource consumption.

crucible.title: The Crucible
crucible.description: 'Concert Hall' taken to the extreme using a maximalist, brute-force reconstruction approach.

correction.label: Error correction
correction.tip: Disabling error correction reduces resource consumption.
